A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated a failure to rescue (FTR) phenomenon in the Italian National Health Service.
we have demonstrated that the failure to rescue (FTR) after rectal cancer surgery is associated with a higher hospital mortality and that it is a source of variation between hospitals.
failure to rescue (FTR) represents a major cause of variation in mortality rates after rectal surgery, which can be reduced by a standardized protocol for postoperative care.
The main takeaway from our work is that
failure to rescue is a significant source of variation in mortality rates after rectal cancer surgery.
there is a lot of room for improvement in the way we care for patients who have had surgery for colorectal cancer, and that we need to be more vigilant about the care we provide to these patients.
the variation in hospital mortality is not due to differences in surgical skill, but to the ability of hospitals to detect complications and to respond appropriately to them.
